extracted.intended_audience: researchers applying for CIHR Project Grants and peer reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and reviewer guidance for assessing CIHR Project Grant applications, covering concept (significance/impact), feasibility (approach, methods, team, resources), contextual considerations, scoring, and EDI/Indigenous health integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance and Impact of the Research (Concept)
rubrics_metrics.description: What is being proposed; Why the project is worth doing; Originality; Anticipated contributions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed under the 'Concept' evaluation component. Reviewers judge the importance of the question, novelty/originality, and the expected contributions or impact of the proposed research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approaches and Methods (Feasibility — HOW and WHEN)
rubrics_metrics.description: Soundness of approach; Methodology; Timeline and milestones; Risk mitigation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed as a Feasibility sub-criterion focusing on whether the proposed methods and timeline are appropriate, rigorous, and feasible; includes explicit consideration of planned milestones and strategies to mitigate risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expertise, Experience, and Resources (Feasibility — WHO and WHERE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualifications of the team; Track record; Available resources; Institutional environment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed as a Feasibility sub-criterion addressing whether the team has the necessary expertise and experience, whether adequate resources are available, and whether the institutional environment supports successful project completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee-based Peer Review Process
rubrics_metrics.description: Group of reviewers with required experience and expertise; Assess quality and potential impact of proposed research; Within the context of the program's objectives
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications are reviewed by committees composed of reviewers selected for relevant expertise. Reviewers evaluate quality and potential impact while considering alignment with the Project Grant program objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextual Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Leave history; Career stage; Areas of research; Experiential knowledge; Diverse career paths; Family responsibilities; Pandemic impact
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must consider applicant context (e.g., leave history, career stage, non-traditional career paths, caregiving responsibilities, pandemic effects) and explicitly account for how these factors may have affected productivity and progress when assessing each criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rating Scale (numerical scoring bands)
rubrics_metrics.description: Score ranges and descriptors: 4.5–4.9 = innovative, filling an important critical gap, with very few flaws and investigators having a comprehensive complement of expertise, experience and resources; 4.0–4.4 = highly competitive, addresses important question; 3.5–3.9 = competitive but with notable weaknesses; 3.0–3.4 = adequate; Below 3.0 = significant weaknesses
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numeric scores are used to quantify reviewers' assessments. Use the provided bands and descriptors to map qualitative judgments about significance, feasibility, investigator complement, and flaws into a numerical score.

rubrics_metrics.name: CIHR Foundation Grants (legacy program) — contrasting criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Different criteria emphasizing: Leadership and significance of research; Research approach and quality; Track record of leadership in field; Mentorship and training of HQP
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a legacy program with distinct emphases (e.g., leadership, mentorship). Useful for understanding differences in assessment priorities between Project Grants and Foundation Grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity, Diversity, Inclusion and Indigenous Health considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Sex and gender-based analysis (SGBA+); Indigenous health research principles; Equity, diversity, and inclusion in research teams; Patient and community engagement (where relevant)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CIHR integrates EDI and Indigenous health principles into review. Reviewers should consider whether SGBA+ has been appropriately applied, whether Indigenous health research principles are followed when relevant, whether team composition reflects EDI, and whether patient/community engagement is included where appropriate.
